method: Literal named columns and stated numeric/text/NULL data; no added constraints or query repairs. Output row order is observed, not guaranteed. Additional queries inspect intermediate rows/truth values separately.

cases.setup: CREATE TABLE T(A); INSERT INTO T VALUES(1),(2),(NULL); CREATE TABLE S(B);

queries.sql: SELECT A FROM T WHERE A NOT IN (SELECT B FROM S WHERE B>0)

cases.setup: CREATE TABLE A(X); INSERT INTO A VALUES(1),(NULL); CREATE TABLE B(Y); INSERT INTO B VALUES(NULL),(2);

queries.sql: SELECT A.X FROM A LEFT JOIN B ON A.X=B.Y WHERE B.Y IS NULL

cases.setup: CREATE TABLE U(V); INSERT INTO U VALUES(1),(1),(2);

queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT V FROM U WHERE V>1
SELECT V FROM U WHERE V>1 GROUP BY V
SELECT V FROM U WHERE V>1

cases.setup: CREATE TABLE P(K); INSERT INTO P VALUES(5),(10); CREATE TABLE Q(K,M); INSERT INTO Q VALUES(5,NULL),(5,1);

queries.sql: SELECT P.K FROM P WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Q WHERE Q.K=P.K AND Q.M>0)

cases.setup: CREATE TABLE L(ID); INSERT INTO L VALUES(10),(20); CREATE TABLE R(ID,X); INSERT INTO R VALUES(20,'a'),(30,'b');

queries.sql: SELECT L.ID, R.X FROM L LEFT JOIN R ON L.ID=R.ID WHERE R.X='a'
SELECT L.ID, R.X FROM L LEFT JOIN R ON L.ID=R.ID
